newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Cofinec says H1 results hit by Hungarian economy.
newsitem.headline: Cofinec says H1 results hit by Hungarian economy.

text.p: France-registered printed packaging materials company Cofinec S.A posted lower net profits in the first six months of 1996 than in the same period of last year primarily due to its performance in Hungary.
"Net profit for this period was 2.1 million French francs, down from 10.3 million French francs in the first half of 1995," Cofinec said in its first half result report on Friday.
"The bulk of this decline is attributable to Petofi's performance," it said.
Cofinec, the first foreign company to be listed on the Budapest Stock Exchange, operates in three central European countries, Hungary, the Czech Republic and Poland.
The group's net sales, calculated according to International Standards, totalled 336.5 million French francs in the January-June period, an increase of 2.7 percent over the first half of 1995.

As expected, the newest operating subsidiary Cofinec Polska, a greenfield development in Poland, did not contribute to consolidated net sales in the first half of 1996, although the loss associated with the Polish operation was less than projected for this start-up period, Cofinec said.
Hungary's macroeconomic performance had a key impact on the figures, the statement said.
"The company's performance during the first half was affected by the one percentage point Gross Domestic Product (GDP) decline in Hungary, Cofinec's major market," it said.

"The ongoing erosion in real wages and retail sales caused several of the company's multinational customers to reduce or suspend production of consumer goods during this period, thereby affecting orders," it added.

Export sales remain an important target area for the group, it said, adding that exports as a percentage of sales increased by 13 percentage points to 9.3 percent of sales, up from 8.2 percent in the first half of 1995.
The company was more optimistic about the second half of the year because the decline in Hungary's GDP is expected to turn around and show improvement by the end of the year.

Further grounds for optimism were the fact that the group's operating subsidiaries are adjusting to new packaging demand patterns and that the lower pricing position in export markets, a necessary temporary measure, will help increase the company's export market share.

Cofinec Polska has now moved into two shift production and received significant order commitments from key multinational consumers, and will contribute to the group's turnover in the third and fourth quarters of 1996, the statement added.

Other positive signs are that following the IPO, Cofinec increased its ownership in its Czech subsidiary, Kpraco, from 50 percent to 100 percent, facilitating further integration of the company into the group.
In addition, debt reduction in the third quarter will reduce interest expenses and estimated 6.6 million French francs in the second half, the statement said.
